q: 1. Pre-cast concrete piles are usually
options: plain, reinforced concrete or pre-stressed concrete
explain: Pre-cast piles must withstand significant tensile stresses during handling, transport, and driving (hammer impact). Therefore, they require either longitudinal reinforcement or pre-stressing to prevent cracking.

q: 2. The length of pre-cast concrete piles varies from
explain: Modern pre-casting and transport capabilities allow for pile lengths up to 30 meters. Lengths beyond this typically require specialized mechanical joints or cast-in-situ methods.

q: 3. In horizontal D.P.C., thickness of cement concrete (1:2:4) is
explain: A standard plinth-level DPC using 1:2:4 concrete is typically 4 cm (approx. 1.5 inches) thick, providing a sufficient barrier against capillary moisture while remaining structurally sound.

q: 4. The formwork from the sides of beams can be removed only after
explain: Vertical formwork (sides of beams/columns) does not support the weight of the concrete; it only holds the shape. It can typically be removed after 24 hours (1 day).

q: 5. The formwork from the slabs excluding props, can be removed only after
explain: According to standard codes (like IS 456), slab soffit formwork can be removed after 3 days, provided the props are immediately re-fixed to support the load.

q: 6. An ordinary concrete may be made water proof by adding
explain: Products like Pudlo and Impermo are integral waterproofing admixtures, while Snowcem is a waterproof cement paint; all are used to enhance the moisture resistance of concrete structures.

q: 7. According to National Building Code, the hydrants in water mains is provided at minimum interval of
explain: Fire safety regulations in the NBC specify that fire hydrants should be placed at intervals no greater than 75 meters to ensure adequate coverage for emergency hoses.

q: 8. The process of hardening the concrete by keeping its surface moist is known
explain: Curing is the maintenance of moisture and temperature conditions to allow concrete to develop its intended strength and durability.

q: 9. Slump used for beam & slab for RCC.
explain: Beams and slabs require medium workability (50-100mm slump) to ensure the concrete flows around dense reinforcement.

q: 10. Slump test in used for
explain: The slump test is a field test used to measure the consistency and workability of fresh concrete.

q: 11. Permissible compressive strength of M 15 concrete grade is
explain: The '15' in M15 refers to its characteristic compressive strength of 15 N/mm², which is equivalent to 150 kg/cm².

q: 12. Water cement ratio for M10 concretes should be
explain: M10 is a lean concrete mix; a water-cement ratio of 0.65 is typically used to ensure enough hydration for this grade.

q: 13. The ratio of various ingredients (cement: sand: aggregates) in concrete of grade M20 is
explain: The standard nominal mix for M20 concrete is 1 part cement, 1.5 parts sand, and 3 parts coarse aggregate (1:1.5:3).

q: 14. The mortar in which both cement and lime are used as binding materials, is called
explain: Gauged mortar is a combination of cement and lime, offering the strength of cement with the workability of lime.

q: 15. The maximum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is that of
explain: Lime (Calcium Oxide) makes up 60-67% of Portland cement, being its primary constituent.

q: 16. The height of slump cone is
explain: The standard dimensions for a slump cone are 30 cm height, 20 cm bottom diameter, and 10 cm top diameter.

q: 17. The unit weight of RCC is taken as
explain: Reinforced Cement Concrete (RCC) has a standard density of 2500 kg/m³, which equals 2.5 t/m³.

q: 18. When first class bricks are immersed in water for one hour, the weight of water absorbed by them should not exceed ..........
explain: First-class bricks should not absorb more than 1/6th (approx. 15-20%) of their dry weight in water after 24 hours of immersion.

q: 19. The advantage of R.C.C. lintel is that ..........
options: the sunshade can be cast monolithic along with lintel
there is no limitation on span
they are strong and fire resistant
explain: RCC lintels are versatile; they allow for integrated sunshades (chajjas), are fireproof, and can be designed for various spans.

q: 20. Temporary structure constructed in a river for excluding water from a given site to enable the building operation to be performed on dry surface is called
explain: A cofferdam is a watertight enclosure pumped dry to allow construction work (like bridge piers) below the waterline.

q: 21. The lower half of the arch between the crown and the skew-back is known as ..........
explain: The haunch is the section of the arch located roughly halfway between the springing point (skewback) and the crown.

q: 22. A continuous series of steps between landings is called ..........
explain: A flight is an uninterrupted sequence of steps between two floor levels or landings.

q: 23. To facilitate draining off rain water from the coping, sills, sunshades, a groove is cut on the underside of these and this groove is known as
explain: Throating (or a drip groove) breaks the surface tension of water, forcing it to drop off the edge rather than running back toward the wall face.

q: 24. In a fact roofed building, the roof is made water proof by coating hot bitumen and this coating is done at the rate of
explain: The standard rate for a single coat of hot bitumen for waterproofing a flat roof surface is 1.65 to 1.67 Kg per square meter.

q: 25. Batching error means in accuracy in the quantity of
explain: Batching is the process of measuring all concrete ingredients; an error in any of these affects the final strength and workability.

q: 26. The upper convex surface of an arch is called as
explain: The extrados is the outer (upper) curved line of an arch, while the intrados is the inner curve.

q: 27. The irregular triangular portion of the arcade, formed between the two arches is called as
explain: Spandrils are the triangular spaces found between adjacent arches or between an arch and a rectangular enclosure.

q: 28. In asbestos cement corrugated sheet roofing, and minimum horizontal lap in metres should be
explain: A 150mm (0.15m) end lap is required to ensure the roof remains watertight during wind-driven rain.

q: 29. As per latest I.S. code the characteristic strength of M 15 grade concrete at 28 days is ..........
explain: In concrete grading (M 15), the number represents the characteristic compressive strength in Newtons per square millimeter (N/mm2).

q: 30. The characteristic strength of a material is defined as the strength below which ..........
options: not more than 5 % of the results fall
not less than 5 % of the results fall
not more than 50 % of the results fall
not more than 25 % of the results fall
explain: The characteristic strength is a statistical value ensuring that 95% of test results meet or exceed the specified strength.

q: 31. The props of from work of the beams with span exceeding 6 m can be removed after ..........
explain: For safety and strength gain, beams with spans over 6 m require props to remain for 21 days according to IS codes.

q: 32. To facilitate quick flow of a rain water on R.C.C. flat roof towards spouts, it is usually given slope of ..........
explain: Flat roofs are never perfectly flat; a slight gradient of 1 in 40 to 1 in 60 (approx 2-3°) is provided to prevent water ponding.

q: 33. Stone chips or broken bricks are also known as ..........
explain: Spalls are small fragments of stone or brick that break off during cutting or due to weathering/impact.

q: 34. Which of the following is not the standard wattage of electrical lamps?
explain: Standard incandescent bulb wattages traditionally follow increments like 40W, 60W, 75W, and 100W; 50W is not a standard incandescent rating.

q: 35. Grade of concrete generally not used in RCC is
explain: M10 is a lean mix used for levelling or mud mats, not for structural reinforced concrete.

q: 36. Which of the following is not the usual size of the ceiling fans?
explain: Standard sweep sizes for ceiling fans are typically 900mm (36"), 1200mm (48"), and 1400mm (56"); 1000mm is uncommon.

q: 37. Depth of lean concrete bed at the bottom of the footing is ..........
options: equal to its projection beyond wall base
equal to half the width of wall in the super structure
explain: The thickness of the lean concrete (PCC) bed is typically made equal to the horizontal offset (projection) to ensure uniform load distribution.

q: 38. If the mortar contains both cement and limes as the binding materials, then it is called ..........
explain: Gauged mortar is a combination of cement and lime, where lime provides workability and cement provides strength and faster setting.

q: 39. The advantage of air entrained concrete in lining walls and roofs is ............
explain: Air-entrained concrete contains tiny air bubbles which reduce thermal conductivity, making it a better heat insulator.

q: 40. In the case of R.C.C. roof slabs covered by insulating layers, the maximum spacing of expansion joints is ..........
explain: For R.C.C. slabs with insulation, the standard spacing for expansion joints is typically between 20 to 30 meters.

q: 41. In the road works the slump of concrete commonly adopted is ..........
explain: Road construction requires very dry or stiff concrete (low workability) to handle heavy compaction, hence a low slump of 20-28 mm is used.

q: 42. A foundation consisting of thick reinforced concrete slab covering the entire area of the bottom of the structure, is known as ..........
explain: A raft or mat foundation is a continuous slab that supports all the columns and walls of a structure.

q: 43. The pre-stressed concrete piles as compared to pre-cast and reinforced concrete piles ..........
explain: Pre-stressed piles are efficient because the high-strength steel and pre-compression allow for smaller sections with higher durability and load capacity.

q: 44. The coefficient of friction between the concrete and soil is ..........
explain: The friction factor (tan δ) for concrete against average soil ranges from 0.30 to 0.35 for design calculations.

q: 45. The center to center spacing of lateral reinforcement in pre-cast reinforced concrete piles should not exceed ........ the least width of the pile.
explain: To prevent buckling of the main bars and to resist driving shocks, the lateral ties are closely spaced at half the pile width.

q: 46. For the pre-cast reinforced concrete piles, the quality of concrete recommended is ..........
explain: M150 to M200 (approx. M15 to M20) is the minimum grade used to ensure the pile can handle the severe stresses of hammer impact.

q: 47. In the pre-cast reinforced concrete piles, the thickness of concrete covering the main bars should not be less than ..........
explain: A minimum clear cover of 40 mm is required for standard piles to protect the reinforcement from soil-based corrosion.

q: 48. The minimum of covering of the reinforcement for the pre-cast reinforced piles used in sea water, is ..........
explain: Due to the highly corrosive nature of chloride in seawater, the cover is increased to 75 mm to prevent the steel from rusting.

q: 49. A temporary structure constructed in a river for excluding water from a given site to enable the building operation to be performed on dry surface, is called ..........
explain: A cofferdam is a temporary enclosure pumped dry to allow construction work (like bridge piers) to take place below the water level.

q: 50. When the depth of water is from 4.5 to 6 m, the type of cofferdam used is ..........
explain: For depths between 4.5 and 6 meters, a double-walled cofferdam provides the necessary stability and water-tightness that simpler earthen or single-walled structures cannot.
